title: Why Num Lock turns off after sleep in Windows 11, and how to keep it on
seo_title: Num Lock Turns Off After Sleep in Windows 11? The Fix
summary: Num Lock keeps turning off after sleep or at the sign-in screen? Why Windows does it, two built-in fixes, and a one-click way.
answer: Windows often resets Num Lock when it wakes up from sleep, and at the sign-in screen it starts with Num Lock off unless you tell it otherwise. The built-in settings below help when the PC starts, but only a small app like AlwaysNumLock keeps it on every time, including after sleep.
body:
You open your laptop, type a phone number on the number pad, and the cursor jumps around instead. Num Lock went off again. It isn't you: Windows forgets it in a few common moments.

## Why Num Lock keeps turning off

1. **After sleep.** Many laptops reset the keyboard when they wake up, and Num Lock goes back to off.
2. **At the sign-in screen.** Windows has its own Num Lock setting for the moment before you sign in, and on most PCs it's off.
3. **After a full shutdown.** With Fast Startup on, Windows doesn't fully restart, and the keyboard often comes back with Num Lock off.
4. **A stray key press.** The `Num Lock` key sits right above `7`, so it's easy to hit by accident.

## Fix 1: turn Num Lock on at the sign-in screen

This tells Windows to start with Num Lock on, so you can type a number PIN straight away. It takes a minute, but you have to be careful because it uses the Registry Editor.

1. Press `Win` + `R`, type **regedit** and press Enter. Click **Yes** when Windows asks.
2. In the bar at the top, paste **HKEY_USERS\.DEFAULT\Control Panel\Keyboard** and press Enter.
3. Double-click **InitialKeyboardIndicators**, change the value to **2** and click **OK**. If the value there is a long number like **2147483648**, change it to **2147483650** instead.
4. Restart your PC.

If it still starts with Num Lock off, try Fix 2.

## Fix 2: turn off Fast Startup

Fast Startup makes Windows start a little quicker, but it also brings the keyboard back the way it was, often with Num Lock off.

1. Open the Start menu, type **Control Panel** and open it.
2. Go to **Hardware and Sound**, then **Power Options**.
3. Click **Choose what the power buttons do**, then **Change settings that are currently unavailable**.
4. Untick **Turn on fast startup** and click **Save changes**.

Some PCs also have a Num Lock option in the BIOS, the settings screen you reach by pressing a key like `F2` or `Del` while the PC starts. If you see **NumLock state**, set it to **On**.

## The easy way: keep it on, always

The fixes above only help when the PC starts. They don't stop Num Lock turning off after sleep, after the lock screen, or when you press the key by accident.

[AlwaysNumLock](/alwaysnumlock/) is a free little app I made for exactly this. It runs quietly next to the clock and keeps Num Lock on in every one of those moments. It can also switch on the sign-in screen setting from Fix 1 for you, with one click and no Registry Editor. Download it, double-click it, and you're done.

Need the number pad as arrow keys for a game? Pause it from its menu by the clock, and turn it back on when you're finished.

title: How to use Caps Lock as copy and paste on Windows
summary: Caps Lock sits in the best spot on your keyboard and does almost nothing. Here's how to make it copy and paste instead.
answer: Windows has no setting to turn Caps Lock into copy and paste. You can remap it to another key with Microsoft PowerToys, but to copy with one tap and paste with two, you need a small app like Capslock-CopyPaste.
body:
Think about how often you press `Ctrl` + `C` and `Ctrl` + `V` in a day. Now think about how often you need CAPITALS that last longer than one word. Caps Lock has the best spot on the keyboard, right under your left little finger, and for most people it's the least useful key there.

## What Windows lets you do

Windows has no built-in setting to change what Caps Lock does. The closest is **Microsoft PowerToys**, a free set of tools from Microsoft. Its **Keyboard Manager** can turn Caps Lock into another single key, like `Ctrl` or `Esc`.

That helps, but it isn't copy and paste: you would still press two keys for each.

## One tap to copy, two taps to paste

This is how I set up my own keyboard:

- Tap `Caps Lock` **once** to copy what you selected.
- Tap it **twice quickly** to paste.
- Press `Ctrl` + `Caps Lock` twice to paste as **plain text**, without the website's fonts and colours.
- Press `Shift` + `Caps Lock` when you really need CAPITALS.

A small note next to your mouse tells you it worked: Copied! or Pasted! If nothing was selected, your old clipboard is kept, so you never lose what you copied before by accident.

It works with text, pictures and files, in every app, including Word, Gmail and File Explorer.

## Set it up

1. Download [Capslock-CopyPaste](/capslock-copypaste/). It's free and there's nothing to install.
2. Double-click the file and click **Yes** when Windows asks.
3. Select some text and tap Caps Lock.

To have it start with your PC, right-click its icon next to the clock and tick **Start with Windows**. Need normal Caps Lock back for a while? Choose **Pause** from the same menu.

title: How to make the Copilot key open Gemini (or ChatGPT) instead
summary: New laptops have a Copilot key that only opens Copilot. Here's how to make it open Gemini, ChatGPT or Claude instead.
answer: Recent versions of Windows 11 let you change the Copilot key, but only to apps from the Microsoft Store, so you can't pick Gemini that way. Install Gemini as an app from Chrome or Edge, then use a small app like Copilot2Gemini to put it on the key.
body:
Most new Windows laptops have a Copilot key next to the space bar. It's a good spot for an AI assistant, but it opens Microsoft Copilot, and many people would rather use Gemini, ChatGPT or Claude.

## Can Windows change it?

Partly. In recent versions of Windows 11 you'll find **Settings**, **Personalization**, **Text input**, **Customize Copilot key on keyboard**. It lets you choose Search or another app, but only apps from the Microsoft Store show up. Gemini in your browser isn't one of them.

## Step 1: install Gemini as an app

This gives Gemini its own window, like a normal app, instead of a browser tab.

1. Open [gemini.google.com](https://gemini.google.com) in Chrome, Edge or Brave.
2. Click the **three-dot menu** at the top right, then **Save and share** (or **Apps**), then **Install page as app**.
3. Click **Install**.

## Step 2: put it on the Copilot key

[Copilot2Gemini](/copilot2gemini/) is a free little app I made for this. It finds the Gemini app you just installed by itself, so there's nothing to set up.

- Press the Copilot key and Gemini opens.
- Press it again and Gemini hides.
- Press it while Gemini is behind other windows and it comes back to the front.

No Copilot key on your keyboard? `Win` + `C` does the same.

## Prefer ChatGPT or Claude?

Install [chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com) or [claude.ai](https://claude.ai) as an app the same way. Then right-click the Copilot2Gemini icon next to the clock, choose **Assistant**, **Rescan installed apps**, and pick the one you want.

title: How to get a clean, minimal new tab page in Chrome
summary: Chrome's new tab page is busy. Here's how to tidy it with Chrome's own settings, or swap it for a calm page with your bookmarks.
answer: Chrome lets you change the new tab background and hide the shortcuts, but not much more. For a calm page with a clock, your own bookmarks and a few notes, use a new tab extension like NN-tab.
body:
You open a new tab dozens of times a day. Each time you see a search box, a row of shortcuts Chrome picked for you, and often news or suggestions you didn't ask for.

## Tidy it with Chrome's own settings

1. Open a new tab and click **Customize Chrome** at the bottom right.
2. Under **Appearance**, pick a plain colour or your own picture.
3. Under **Shortcuts**, choose **My shortcuts** to pick your own, or turn shortcuts off.

That's about all Chrome lets you change. You can't add notes, sort sites into groups, or remove the big search box.

## A calmer page instead

[NN-tab](/nn-tab/) is a free extension I made to replace the new tab page with something quiet:

- A big, clear clock with the date.
- Your favourite sites as tiles, sorted into groups like Work and Social.
- A short to-do list.
- A quote you like, and your own wallpaper.

Everything stays on your computer. There's no account and no tracking.

## Add it to Chrome

NN-tab isn't in the Chrome Web Store yet, so you add it yourself. It takes two minutes: download it, unzip it, open **chrome://extensions**, turn on **Developer mode** and click **Load unpacked**. The [NN-tab page](/nn-tab/) shows each step.

It works in Edge and Brave too.

title: YouTube ambient mode is too subtle? A stronger glow, and a fixed video quality
seo_title: YouTube Ambient Mode: Stronger Glow and Fixed Quality
summary: YouTube's ambient mode is faint and quality keeps changing. Here's what YouTube's own settings do, and how to get more.
answer: YouTube's own ambient mode only works in dark theme and is very soft, and YouTube changes the video quality as it likes. The ytModify extension adds a stronger glow that works in full screen, and keeps the quality you choose for each view.
body:
Two small things make YouTube feel worse than it should: the glow around the video is barely there, and the quality keeps dropping to something blurry.

## What YouTube gives you

**Ambient mode** adds a soft glow around the video in the colours of what's playing. Turn it on from the gear icon under a video, but it only shows in dark theme, it's very faint, and it switches off in full screen.

**Video quality** can be set for one video from the same gear icon. For all videos, YouTube's settings only offer broad choices like **Higher picture quality** or **Data saver**, not a fixed resolution.

## A stronger glow, and the quality you choose

[ytModify](/ytmodify/) is a free Chrome extension I put together for this. It adds:

- **Ambient light** that follows the video's colours, in normal view and full screen. It can also hide black bars.
- **A fixed quality for each view**, for example 1080p in full screen, 720p normally and 360p in the mini player.
- **A bigger player**, YouTube's own font and coloured highlights.
- **Auto pop-out**: the video floats in a small window when you switch tabs.

Everything is set from one small window, and changes show up straight away. Press `G` while watching to turn the glow on or off.

## Add it to Chrome

Download it from the [ytModify page](/ytmodify/), unzip it, open **chrome://extensions**, turn on **Developer mode** and click **Load unpacked**. The page shows each step.

title: How to keep YouTube playing in a small window when you switch tabs
seo_title: Keep YouTube Playing in a Small Window (Auto PiP)
summary: Chrome can float a YouTube video in a small window, but you have to start it by hand. Here's how to make it happen by itself.
answer: Chrome has picture-in-picture built in: right-click a YouTube video twice and choose Picture in picture. To make it happen by itself every time you switch tabs, use an extension like ytModify.
body:
You're watching a video and need to check something in another tab. The moment you switch, the video is gone from view. Picture-in-picture fixes that: the video floats in a small window in the corner while you do something else.

## The built-in way

1. On a YouTube video, **right-click twice**. The first right-click shows YouTube's menu, the second shows Chrome's.
2. Choose **Picture in picture**.

You can also click the **media controls** icon in Chrome's toolbar while a video plays and press the picture-in-picture button there.

Either way, you have to do it every time.

## Make it happen by itself

[ytModify](/ytmodify/), a free Chrome extension I made, does it for you:

- Switch to another tab and the playing video pops out into a small window.
- Come back to YouTube and it slides back into the page.
- A paused video stays where it is.

Switching to another app instead of another tab? Press `P` first. Chrome only pops a video out by itself when you change tabs, so the key does it before you switch.

You can turn the pop-out on or off, and choose whether it also works on Shorts, in ytModify's settings.

## Add it to Chrome

Download it from the [ytModify page](/ytmodify/), unzip it, open **chrome://extensions**, turn on **Developer mode** and click **Load unpacked**.

title: Want to cut down on a habit? Start by counting it
summary: Smoking, junk food, endless scrolling: before you can cut down, you need to know how often it really happens. A one-tap way to count.
answer: Counting a habit honestly is one of the simplest ways to cut down, because you see the real number instead of a guess. Keep it private and fast: one tap each time, and a monthly limit to aim for.
body:
Most of us guess how often we do the thing we're trying to cut down on, and most of us guess low. Smoking, drinking, junk food, scrolling at night: the real number is usually a surprise.

## Why counting helps

- **You see the truth.** A number is harder to argue with than a feeling.
- **You notice the moment.** Reaching for your phone to count makes you pause, and sometimes that pause is enough.
- **You can see progress.** A slightly better week is easy to miss without a record.

## Make it easy, or you'll stop

Counting only works if it takes a second and nobody else sees it. A notes app is slow, and a fitness app wants an account. What helps most:

1. **One tap** each time it happens, nothing to type.
2. **A monthly limit** you choose, so you have something to aim for.
3. **A quick look at the week**, compared with the week before.
4. **Privacy**, with a PIN and nothing stored online.

## The app I made for this

[How Many Times](/how-many-time/) is a free app that does exactly that. There's one big button to tap when you slip, a heart for each month that drains as you get closer to your limit, and a chart of your last seven days.

It runs in your browser, on your phone or computer, with no sign-up. Everything stays on your device, locked with your PIN. Add it to your home screen and it opens like a normal app, even without internet.

Be kind to yourself when the number is high. The point isn't a perfect month: it's a slightly better one than last time.

title: Sending money from Romania to Bangladesh: how the 2.5% incentive works
seo_title: Romania to Bangladesh Remittance: The 2.5% Incentive
summary: Bangladesh adds 2.5% to money sent home the legal way. What that means, and how to work out exactly what arrives.
answer: When you send money to Bangladesh through a bank or a licensed service like Remitly, the government adds 2.5% on top of the converted amount. So 10,000 taka converted becomes 10,250 taka when it arrives. Money sent through informal hundi gets nothing extra.
body:
If you work in Romania or elsewhere in Europe and send money home, there's a bonus you should count on: Bangladesh's government remittance incentive.

## What the incentive is

Bangladesh adds **2.5%** to money sent home through legal channels: a bank, or a licensed money transfer service like Remitly or Western Union. It's added to the taka your family receives, and you don't have to apply for it.

Money sent through informal hundi doesn't get it. For larger amounts, the bank in Bangladesh may ask for some documents before paying the incentive.

## Working it out

There are two steps:

1. **Convert** what you send to taka at the exchange rate.
2. **Add 2.5%** on top.

For example, sending **500 RON** at a rate of 25.88 taka per leu:

- 500 x 25.88 = **12,940 TK** converted
- 2.5% incentive = **323.50 TK**
- Arrives in Bangladesh: **13,263.50 TK**

Working backwards is trickier. If your family needs exactly 10,000 TK, you divide by 1.025 first: you only need to send enough for about 9,756 TK, because the incentive adds the rest.

## Let the calculator do it

My [currency converter](/currency-converter/) does both directions for Romanian leu and euro, with today's rate filled in. Type what you'll send, or what should arrive, and it shows the converted amount, the incentive and the total.

Before you pay, check the rate your bank or app gives you, since it can be a little different from today's market rate. You can type it into the calculator instead.

title: How to copy text from a photo or screenshot on Windows
summary: Need the words from a photo, a paused video or a scanned PDF? Here are the quickest ways to copy them on Windows, Bangla included.
answer: On Windows 11, Snipping Tool can copy text from a screenshot with Text actions, and Microsoft PowerToys adds a Text Extractor for any part of the screen. For photos, videos and Bangla text, a free app like QuickNotes copies it with a double-tap of Right Alt.
body:
You've got a photo of a poster, a screenshot of a booking or a paused video with the exact words you need. You can see the text, but you can't select it, so you end up typing it out letter by letter. There are faster ways.

## What Windows can already do

- **Snipping Tool** (Windows 11): take a screenshot with `Win` + `Shift` + `S`, open it in Snipping Tool and click **Text actions**. You can then select the words or click **Copy all text**. It's built in, but it's a few clicks every time.
- **PowerToys Text Extractor**: Microsoft's free PowerToys adds a shortcut, `Win` + `Shift` + `T`, that lets you draw a box anywhere on the screen and copies the text inside it. It reads English and other languages Windows supports well.
- **Google Lens in Chrome**: right-click a picture on a website and choose **Search image with Google Lens**, then pick **Text**. Handy for images online, less so for photos on your PC.

These work fine for clean English text. They struggle with blurry photos, handwriting-style fonts and languages like Bangla, where most built-in readers return a jumble of letters.

## Copy text from a photo, step by step

1. Open the photo, video or PDF so the text is on your screen. Pause the video on the right frame.
2. Zoom in if the text is small. Bigger text is read more accurately by every tool.
3. Use one of the tools above, or the easy way below, and draw a tight box around just the words you want.
4. Paste with `Ctrl` + `V` and check numbers and names before you send them on.

## Text you normally can't copy

A few places where this saves the most time:

- A phone number or address in a photo someone sent on WhatsApp.
- A recipe, a slide or subtitles in a paused YouTube video.
- A scanned PDF where nothing can be selected.
- An error message on screen that you want to search for.

## The easy way: double-tap Right Alt

I wanted this to take one second, so I made [QuickNotes](/quicknotes/), a free little Windows app. Tap `Right Alt` twice, drag over any text on your screen, and it's copied. It reads photos, videos, PDFs and apps, in Bangla, English, Hindi and more, because it uses Google Gemini to read the text.

1. Download [QuickNotes](/quicknotes/) and double-click the file. There's nothing to install.
2. The first time, it helps you get a **free Gemini key** in about a minute: click **Open AI Studio**, then **Create API key**, then **Test** and **Save**.
3. Double-tap `Right Alt`, drag a box, and paste.

Right Alt keeps working as normal; only a quick double-tap starts a scan. One honest note: only the box you drag is sent to Google, but on the free plan Google may use it to improve its products, so don't scan passwords or bank details.
